sampling_model.design: One aggregate unit is assigned by a known sequential kernel \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\); the comparison class includes deterministic, history-dependent, and outcome-adaptive rules.
sampling_model.units: A single fixed finite-population trajectory of length \(T\); no unit, outcome, or state is sampled from a superpopulation.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment \(W_t\in\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\) is randomized over time, and assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.overlap: No positivity condition is imposed on the minimax policy class. The constructive Markov design has homogeneous-history exposure probability exceeding \(1/(2\mathrm e)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no stochastic outcome nuisances. The known quantities are \(T\), \(B\), \(C\), and \(\beta\); unknown-index adaptation is outside scope.

body.tldr: The constructive side is now an exact finite-horizon radius-aware certificate: optimize the audited Markov truncated Horvitz--Thompson bound over integer windows and cap it by the zero estimator's \(4B^2\) risk.  The certified window is constant when \(C/B\) is below the \(T^{-1/2}\) elbow, has scale \(\{(C/B)^2T\}^{1/(2\beta+1)}\) in the intermediate regime, and saturates at the horizon when \(C/B\) reaches order \(T^\beta\).  The policy-uniform converse remains open: the common-null calculations do not yet prove even the proposed \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) multiscale certificate, so the displayed matched frontier is explicitly conditional.  The \(C=0\) boundary retains the ordinary parametric frontier.

project_justification.gap: Finite-order regular-design optimization, geometric-mixing analyses, and recent sequential rerandomization do not supply a policy-uniform common-null information certificate for fixed-array polynomial memory.  The optimized Markov construction gives a radius-aware all-horizon upper certificate, but no proved deterministic occupancy--information inequality currently rules out a better outcome-adaptive policy, even with the candidate dyadic logarithmic loss.
project_justification.niche: Known beta removes adaptation to the decay index from scope. For the constructive nonadaptive design, exposure variance grows with the homogeneous-history window while deterministic carryover bias decays polynomially. Any benefit from outcome-adaptive assignment remains unresolved and is the subject of the open sequential multiscale-certificate question.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution in the present core is the optimized radius-aware Markov certificate, including the trivial bounded-parameter cap and the low-, intermediate-, and high-memory elbows.  The common-null horizon-eight calculation isolates the prospective converse mechanism, while the general all-policy multiscale certificate and both its logarithmic and no-log forms remain open rather than being promoted as results.

body.related_work: Bojinov, Simchi-Levi, and Zhao analyze exact-\(m\), regular switchback designs and optimize Horvitz--Thompson risk; their result informs the constructive architecture here but is not an all-policy or arbitrary-estimator converse.  Hu and Wager study geometrically mixing Markov dynamics, whose stochastic contraction does not imply the fixed-array polynomial-memory certificate sought here.  Jia, Kallus, and Yu provide a truncated-exposure estimation template under rapid mixing and graph clustering, again informing the upper audit rather than the open converse.  Duchi and Ruan's constrained-risk inequality can be used only after close adaptive trajectory laws have been constructed and supplies no switchback occupancy inequality.  Zeng and coauthors study sequential rerandomization under no or first-order carryover.  Xiong, Chin, and Taylor inform the operational window interpretation.  Lin and Ding and Liu and Zhong address separate inference problems.  None of these comparisons is used to claim that the open all-policy multiscale certificate has been proved.
body.interpretation: For a pre-registered experiment with known \(B\), \(C\), and \(\beta\), the constructive recommendation is to minimize the displayed finite list of \(T\) audited certificates.  In the intermediate regime this means a clock-time window proportional to \(d\{(C/B)^2T\}^{1/(2\beta+1)}\); weak memory calls for a constant window, while sufficiently strong memory drives the Markov certificate to a horizon-scale window and leaves the universal \(4B^2\) cap as the safer guarantee.  Because the sequential converse is open, these prescriptions are certified upper-bound choices, not yet information-theoretically necessary windows.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The general-horizon prior family is now enumerated and its support, exact randomized-offset block posterior payoff, arm-specific endpoint displacement, structural trajectory factorization, and reverse divergence bound are proved.  The remaining obstruction is a common-measure dyadic stopping argument: the block payoff is averaged under \(\overline Q_b^{\mathrm{blk}}\), while band information is averaged under \(Q_0^{T,L}\).  Assignment-kernel cancellation does not itself transfer occupancy expectations between these laws, and the block perturbation need not have uniformly bounded divergence from the null.  Thus neither the proposed \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) certificate nor its no-log refinement is currently a theorem.
body.honest_scope: The optimized Markov upper certificate, its explicit finite-horizon constants, its \(4B^2\) cap, and its radius-aware operational elbows are proved.  The all-policy common-null converse, including the proposed \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) version with radius term \(B^2\wedge C^2L^{-2\beta}\), remains open; the no-log frontier theorem is only a conditional implication.  The no-carryover boundary is retained separately.  No unknown-\(\beta\) adaptation, confidence interval, policy-optimality certificate, or sharp leading constant is claimed.
